subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] mm/swap: move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator

2026-08-21.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a new page into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator, allowing callers to control when the page is added to the LRU. This change is necessary because the next patch needs to evaluate the refault of a swapped-in page before it becomes visible to reclaim, and adding the page to the LRU too early would interfere with this process. The swap cache allocator now returns a locked folio that is not on the LRU, allowing callers to add it to the LRU when they are ready.

reviews.author: Barry Song
reviews.summary: Raised concern about duplicate patches and lack of clarity in cover letter. Asked for explanation, but no further discussion on the technical aspects of the patch.
reviews.raw_body:
On Fri, Aug 21, 2026 at 5:37 PM Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr> wrote:
>
> The swap cache allocator adds the new folio to the LRU itself, which
> forces every caller to live with that ordering.  The next patch needs to
> evaluate the refault of a swapped-in folio *before* it becomes visible to
> reclaim, because folio_add_lru() consumes PG_workingset/PG_active when it
> picks the LRU list (and, under MGLRU, the generation).
>
> So defer the LRU addition to the callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(),
> no functional change intended.
>
> Suggested-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>
> Signed-off-by: Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr>

Hi Alexandre,

I’m getting a bit confused, as I noticed that you also have this
patch in another patchset:

https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20260818163221.589352-2-alex@ghiti.fr/

Why are you including the same patch in two different patchsets?

Thanks
Barry

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary: Clarified that the patch was included in two different patchsets due to a mistake and explained that it is not relevant to the technical discussion. Mentioned that Sashiko's review on v1 pointed out an issue with MGLRU folio placement, but this will be addressed in a future patch.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Barry,

On Sun, Aug 23, 2026 at 10:39 AM Barry Song <baohua@kernel.org> wrote:
>
> >
> On Fri, Aug 21, 2026 at 5:37 PM Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr> wrote:
> >
> > The swap cache allocator adds the new folio to the LRU itself, which
> > forces every caller to live with that ordering.  The next patch needs to
> > evaluate the refault of a swapped-in folio *before* it becomes visible to
> > reclaim, because folio_add_lru() consumes PG_workingset/PG_active when it
> > picks the LRU list (and, under MGLRU, the generation).
> >
> > So defer the LRU addition to the callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(),
> > no functional change intended.
> >
> > Suggested-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>
> > Signed-off-by: Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr>
>
> Hi Alexandre,
>
> I’m getting a bit confused, as I noticed that you also have this
> patch in another patchset:
>
> https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20260818163221.589352-2-alex@ghiti.fr/
>
> Why are you including the same patch in two different patchsets?

Sorry for the confusion, I explained it in the cover letter but should
have explicitly answered Sashiko's review on v1.

Sashiko pointed out that moving workingset_refault() out of
__swap_cache_alloc_folio() breaks MGLRU folio placement:

"swap_cache_alloc_folio() calls folio_add_lru() which places the folio
in the per-CPU lru addition batch. If this batch drains before
workingset_refault() executes, lru_gen_add_folio() calculates the
generation without PG_workingset being set, placing the folio in an older,
suboptimal generation."

https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260817144622.137133-1-alex%40ghiti.fr

But good news is that v5 of dropbehing will drop this patch :)

Thanks, Barry, for all your comments.

Alex

>
> Thanks
> Barry
>

2026-08-23.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve the swap cache allocator by moving LRU insertion out of it, allowing callers to control when a folio is added to the LRU. This change is necessary for evaluating refaults and reclaiming swapped-in folios correctly. The first patch in the series makes this change without introducing any functional changes.
